title: Goal manipulation through policy-like language in invoice content
summary: Same sink and effect as FB-01. An invoice that should go to human review is approved for payment.

LC.rationale: Attacker-controlled invoice description text enters model context via the get_invoice_details tool result, i.e., through ingested content rather than a direct instruction channel.

CP.rationale: Each invoice starts a fresh message list; attacker text is only re-retrieved per request with no durable agent memory or standing-behaviour alteration.

AP.rationale: The injected directive influences tool selection within the single FinBot agent under one principal and policy domain; no other agent or trust boundary is crossed.

RH.rationale: The CTF flag-awarding logic (finbot_agent.py:119-138) is on the agent's path via approve_invoice, but only a prose walkthrough exists and no human-verified reward-hacking episode is shown.

ES.rationale: Five fixed tools defined in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills; tool binding is allowlisted outside model output.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice processor whose goals and approve/reject/escalate decisions are natural-language tool calls chosen by the model.
